HowTo.Title: How to use
HowTo.WhatItDoes1: Valve games like Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2 and Deadlock connect you to game servers through Valve's relay network (Steam Datagram Relay). Steam Route Tool lets you block relays in specific locations with Windows Firewall, so matchmaking only puts you on the servers you want, for example only nearby ones.
HowTo.Step1: 1. Pick your game at the top of the Routes page. The route list comes from Steam and is always current.
HowTo.Step2: 2. Wait for the pings to fill in. Green is under 50 ms, amber under 100 ms, red above.
HowTo.Step3: 3. Tick **Blocked** on every route you don't want to play on. The firewall rule is created immediately.
HowTo.Step4: 4. Start (or restart) matchmaking in the game. Blocked locations aren't used anymore.
HowTo.Step5: 5. When you're done, use **Unblock all** to remove every rule, or leave them: they stay until you change them. To block only while the app is open, turn on **Unblock all routes when closing** in Settings.
HowTo.Blocking1: **Only play in one region:** choose the region (for example Europe) in the region filter and click **Block all except shown**. Every other route is blocked and the shown ones are unblocked. This works with the search box too.
HowTo.Blocking2: **Let the app choose:** click the blue **Auto select** button to keep the 5 fastest routes and block all others. Use the arrow next to it to keep more or fewer routes (with a preview), and **Undo** in the confirmation if you change your mind. It uses each route's best known ping; blocked routes can't be pinged, so for them the last measured ping is used. For the most accurate result, click **Unblock all** and **Ping all** first.
HowTo.Blocking3: **Individual relays:** most locations have several relay servers. Click the arrow next to a route to show them and block single relays. A route with only some relays blocked shows a filled checkbox (■).
HowTo.Blocking4: **Sorting and filtering:** click a column header to sort by name, region, relay count, ping or blocked state. Use the search box, the region and status filters, or turn off **Group by region** for one flat list.
HowTo.Presets1: A preset is a named set of blocked routes, for example "EU blocked" or "Warsaw only". Block the routes you want, click the save button next to **Preset** at the top of the Routes page, type a name and click **Save**. Each game has its own presets.
HowTo.Presets2: Pick a preset in the **Preset** list to block exactly its routes and unblock all others; **Undo** brings back what was blocked before. The list shows which preset matches what's blocked now, or "No preset" once you change something. You can also switch presets from the tray icon's menu.
HowTo.Presets3: To update a preset, block the routes you want and save again under its name. Rename a preset by editing its name in the same panel, or delete it with the bin button. A route saved as fully blocked stays fully blocked even if Valve adds relays to it later.
HowTo.Profiles1: Each game remembers its own blocked routes. When you switch games, that game's saved selection is applied to the firewall automatically.
HowTo.Profiles2: Valve's games share the same relay servers, and firewall rules apply to your whole PC. Blocking a route for one game therefore blocks it for every game until you switch profiles or unblock it.
HowTo.Pings1: Greyed values are from your last session and are replaced as fresh results arrive. A collapsed route shows the best ping of its relays. **no reply** means none of the tried relays answered; **blocked** routes aren't pinged because their pings are blocked too. Click any ping to measure it again.
HowTo.Pings2: Pings are sent quickly in a first round and anything that didn't answer is retried one at a time. Some routers (flood protection) and ISPs drop replies when many pings are sent at once; on such networks the list fills in over 10–20 seconds.
HowTo.Background1: Turn on **Minimize to tray** in Settings to keep the app out of the taskbar: minimizing hides the window and leaves an icon in the notification area (on Windows 10 it may be behind the ^ arrow; drag it onto the taskbar to keep it visible). Click the icon to open the window, or right-click it to switch games and presets, run Auto select, unblock all routes or exit.
HowTo.Background2: Turn on **Start with Windows** to start the app minimized when you sign in. This is useful together with **Unblock all routes when closing**, which only blocks routes while the app is running. Starting the app again while it's already running brings back the open window.
HowTo.Troubleshooting1: **"Couldn't update the Windows Firewall rules":** the tool needs administrator rights (Windows asks when it starts) and the Windows Defender Firewall service must be running. Third-party firewalls that replace Windows Firewall aren't supported.
HowTo.Troubleshooting2: **Still connected to a blocked location:** blocking only affects new connections. Leave the match and search again.
HowTo.Troubleshooting3: **Seeing the rules:** open Windows Defender Firewall (Settings → Open Windows Firewall) → Outbound Rules. The rules are named SteamRouteTool-UDP/TCP/ICMP-<route> and grouped under SteamRouteTool.
HowTo.Troubleshooting4: **Windows protected your PC:** the download isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn the first time. Choose More info, then Run anyway.
HowTo.Removing1: Click **Unblock all** first, so no firewall rules are left behind, and turn off **Start with Windows** in Settings. Then delete the program and, if you like, its settings folder:
